title: How do you present your structure in a case interview?
description: Interviewers weigh it heavily. Your structure is your plan for the whole case. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
hook: This is the moment you lay out how you will solve the problem. It is the stage people practise most, and still the one that goes wrong most often. Here is how to do it calmly.
body:
Stage 4 of 10 in the ten stages of a case.

Why it matters

Interviewers weigh it heavily. Your structure is your plan for the whole case.

The common mistake

Generic buckets that would fit any company, and no hypothesis.

What to do, and what to say

Draw it

3-4 first-level buckets; under each, short second-level drivers tailored to THIS client.

Check it is MECE

Before speaking: do buckets overlap? Is anything big missing, like regulation, competition or industry-wide effects? Use factors for "why" questions, steps for "should we" questions.

Present it top-down

Big points first. Number them. Say which matters most and end with a hypothesis.

"There are three areas I want to look at. First... I believe the second, the unit economics, is most likely the issue, so I’d start there."

Practise the moment

Read the situation and say your answer out loud before you open the model.

You’ve drawn a three-bucket structure for a market entry case. Present it.

Show a strong answer

"There are three areas I want to look at. First, whether the market is attractive; second, whether we can win against incumbents; third, whether the economics work. I believe the second is the deciding factor because the market is crowded, so I’d start there."

Why it works: Top-down, numbered, prioritised, and ending with a hypothesis.

You finish presenting your structure. What do you NOT say?

Show a strong answer

Not: "Where would you like me to start?" Instead: "I believe X is most likely the issue, because... Do we have data on that?"

Why it works: Stating a hypothesis shows you’re solving the problem, not just organising it.

Next stage: lead the case.
outro: Practise stage 4 with flashcards on the free perfect casing page. Next in this topic: How do you lead a case by proposing the next step?
